title: NSIC Rc 556 (Salinas 32) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 556 is an inbred rice for saline prone fields: about 129 days and 2.6 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 556 is an inbred rice variety for saline prone fields, known locally as Salinas 32. The NSIC approved it in 2019. IRRI bred it. It matures in about 129 days and averages 2.6 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 4.2 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 556, or Rc 556, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 556 yield?

On average it gives 2.6 tonnes per hectare. That is about 52 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 48 saline prone fields inbreds on the list, which is 2.9 tonnes. But the top yield, 4.2 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 129 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as medium duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits fields where salt reaches the soil, such as coastal paddies. So flush the field with fresh water before planting when you can. Our guide to [saline soil preparation](/land-preparation/saline-soil-preparation) shows what helps. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 556?
items.a: It is known as Salinas 32. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 556 take to harvest?
items.a: About 129 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 556?
items.a: It averages 2.6 tonnes per hectare, about 52 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 4.2 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against tungro, sheath blight. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
